name: Two Endpoint Repairs Produce a Terminal Cut-Vertex Obstruction
statement: Let $(C,0)$ be an irredundantly embedded rooted factor whose only corner is $0$. Let $A=C\cup\{\alpha\}$ and $D=C\cup\{\delta\}$ be distinct ample one-concept extensions such that $A,D,A\cup D$ are ample, both extensions peel to $0$, and their shadows intersect in $\operatorname{Sh}(C)$. The paired square construction is a rooted factor $Y$ with exactly three corners: its root and the two repair tips. Deleting either nonroot corner destroys rooted minimality. Gluing $(Y,a)$ to a disjoint copy of $(C,0)$ gives a corner-descent-terminal ample pc-minimal obstruction $X$ with a cut vertex, exactly two corners, and $|X|=4|C|+2$. It has no nontrivial replicated common-seed presentation with resolving tips.
proof: Paired-square transfer makes $Y$ a rooted factor and gives its exact corners after any subset of the two tips is deleted. Removing either tip turns one side section back into $C$; a new-coordinate restriction followed by contraction exposes the bad rooted minor $(C,0)$, so rooted minimality fails. The cut-vertex classification makes $X=Y\vee C$ ample and pc-minimal outside dismantlable ampleness. The glued root is no longer a corner, leaving exactly the two tips. After either tip deletion, a proper minor is the nonpeelable double $C\vee C$, proving terminality. Replicated common-seed constructions with resolving tips are two-connected, while $X$ has a cut vertex.
